why: The profile can finish correctly and still yield nothing if the parent that collects its result is gone. A crashed Gradle daemon would leave the JVM running with no one to read its exit status, and the report file would be written but never consumed.
chain: PID 26128, the profile JVM, working set 8.54 GB
PID 33324, the Gradle daemon, working set 0.87 GB
PID 40784, 35556, 25796 and 18680, the gradlew wrapper chain
implication: Three links matter. The JVM produces the verdict, the daemon collects the task result and writes the build outcome, and the wrapper chain is the caller still waiting. With all present, the profile's ending will be observed and recorded rather than orphaned.
resourceSanity: The profile JVM sits at 8.54 GB working set against an 8 GB -Xmx, and the daemon at 0.87 GB. Neither has grown unexpectedly across the run.
whatWouldHaveBrokenIt: Killing a Gradle process mid-run would orphan the JVM. Nothing in this session has done so, and the guard added to Test-S5Release.ps1 exists precisely to stop that script's initial gradle clean from deleting the live run directory.
